bug_description.normalized: The PoC is a glTF JSON document whose only image URI is `data:image/gif;base64,VAEJ090AABBhesvwBwAJ0RB`. `DecodeDataURI()` base64-decodes that suffix into 17 bytes `54 01 09 d3 dd 00 00 10 61 7a cb f0 07 00 09 d1 10`, `ParseImage()` passes those bytes unchanged to `tinygltf::LoadImageData()`, and `stbi_load_from_memory()` content-sniffs them as TGA rather than GIF. In `stbi__tga_load()`, the decoded header yields `tga_indexed = 1`, `tga_image_type = 9`, `tga_palette_len = 0`, `tga_palette_bits = 16`, `tga_width = 7`, `tga_height = 53513`, and `tga_bits_per_pixel = 16`. The indexed-TGA path derives `tga_comp = 3` from the 16-bit palette entries, allocates `tga_palette` from `tga_palette_len * tga_comp = 0`, then later forces the first palette index to `0` because `pal_idx >= tga_palette_len` is necessarily true when the palette length is zero. The subsequent `raw_data[j] = tga_palette[pal_idx+j];` copies three bytes from that empty palette and reproduces the saved AddressSanitizer `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 3` at `stb_image.h:5643`; the ASan allocation trace shows the palette allocation at line 5590 returned a 1-byte region. The staged fix hunk adds `if (tga_palette_len == 0) { ... return stbi__errpuc("bad palette", "Corrupt TGA"); }` immediately before palette allocation, which is the missing guard this trace exposes.

source.description: First project statement that turns the attacker-controlled image URI payload into raw image bytes later handed to stb_image.
source.value_from: The PoC JSON at `gt_results/arvo_35426/poc` contains `images[0].uri == "data:image/gif;base64,VAEJ090AABBhesvwBwAJ0RB"`; this branch base64-decodes that suffix into the exact 17 bytes `54 01 09 d3 dd 00 00 10 61 7a cb f0 07 00 09 d1 10`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The indexed-TGA decoder copies three RGB bytes from `tga_palette` into `raw_data`, but here the palette is empty.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 3` at `stbi__tga_load /src/tinygltf/.../stb_image.h:5643:31`, and the corresponding allocation trace points back to the palette allocation at line 5590.

root_cause.description: The indexed-TGA palette-loading path does not reject `tga_palette_len == 0` before allocating and later indexing `tga_palette`.
root_cause.note: The staged fix inserts `if (tga_palette_len == 0) { ... return stbi__errpuc("bad palette", "Corrupt TGA"); }` immediately before this allocation, expressing the missing obligation.

tainted_value_origin.description: The decoded payload is copied into the `img` byte vector and given exact extent `img.size() == 17`; later code passes this `(bytes,size)` pair into `stb_image` unchanged.

parser_admitted.description: Content sniffing accepts the decoded payload as TGA and dispatches into `stbi__tga_load`, even though the enclosing data URI advertises `image/gif`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The PoC's `images[0].uri` begins with `data:image/gif;base64,`, so this branch decodes the suffix `VAEJ090AABBhesvwBwAJ0RB` into the 17 raw image bytes `54 01 09 d3 dd 00 00 10 61 7a cb f0 07 00 09 d1 10`.

Immediately after `out->resize(data.size())`, the same 17 decoded bytes are copied into the caller-owned vector `img`. This materializes the exact `(img.data(), img.size() == 17)` buffer later handed to the image loader callback.
`ParseImage()` passes `&img.at(0)` and `static_cast<int>(img.size())` from step 1 as `bytes` and `size`, so stb_image receives the same 17-byte payload. The URI MIME label is not consulted here.

stb_image content-sniffs the buffer. `stbi__tga_test(s)` consumes the 17 supplied bytes and accepts them as TGA because they parse as `tga_color_type = 1`, `tga_image_type = 9`, palette-entry size `16`, positive width `7`, positive height `0xd109`, and index bpp `16`, so `stbi__load_main` dispatches into `stbi__tga_load` despite the enclosing `image/gif` URI label.

fine_trace.var: tga_indexed, tga_image_type, tga_palette_len, tga_palette_bits, tga_width, tga_height, tga_bits_per_pixel
fine_trace.note: The TGA loader re-parses header fields from the attacker-controlled payload. For this witness they become `tga_indexed = 1`, `tga_image_type = 9`, `tga_palette_start = 0xddd3`, `tga_palette_len = 0`, `tga_palette_bits = 16`, `tga_width = 7`, `tga_height = 0xd109`, and `tga_bits_per_pixel = 16`.

Because the image is indexed and the palette entry size is 16 bits, `stbi__tga_get_comp()` maps the palette to `tga_comp = STBI_rgb` (3 bytes) and sets `tga_rgb16 = 1`. Those derived values control both palette allocation size and the later three-byte copy into `raw_data`.

Root cause. The indexed-palette path runs even though step 4 set `tga_palette_len = 0`; there is no zero-entry guard before allocation. This computes a logical palette size of `0 * 3` bytes and still returns a non-null palette pointer; the saved ASan allocation trace shows the resulting region was only 1 byte wide.

The pixel loop executes because step 4 gave positive dimensions (`7 * 0xd109 > 0`). On its first iteration `stbi__tga_load` reads a 16-bit palette index; no pixel bytes remain after the 17-byte witness, so `stbi__get16le(s)` falls through to two EOF `stbi__get8()` returns of `0` and yields `pal_idx = 0`.

With `tga_palette_len == 0`, this condition is true for any palette index value, including the `0` from step 7. Instead of rejecting the empty palette, the decoder forces `pal_idx` to `0`, making the later lookup appear in-range.
Converts palette entry index `0` into byte offset `0 * 3 = 0`, so the subsequent read starts at the beginning of `tga_palette` and spans three RGB bytes.

Sink. The loop runs for `j = 0..2` because `tga_comp == 3`, so it reads three bytes from `tga_palette[0..2]`. The saved ASan trace reports that `tga_palette` was only a 1-byte allocation from step 6, so this three-byte copy is the observed heap-buffer-overflow READ 3.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of a 1-byte region allocated here via `stbi__malloc_mad2(tga_palette_len, tga_comp, 0)`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.dedup_token: __asan_memcpy--stbi__tga_load(stbi__context*, int*, int*, int*, int, stbi__result_info*)--stbi__load_main(stbi__context*, int*, int*, int*, int, stbi__result_info*, int)
sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Yes. The staged fix adds `if (tga_palette_len == 0) { ... return stbi__errpuc("bad palette", "Corrupt TGA"); }` immediately before the vulnerable palette allocation in `stbi__tga_load()`, so this exact zero-entry indexed-palette witness is rejected before `tga_palette` can be allocated and read.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_35426 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 3 in stbi__tga_load` with stack `stbi__tga_load -> stbi__load_main -> stbi__load_and_postprocess_8bit`.

format.name: glTF JSON with one `data:image/gif` URI whose payload is a 17-byte indexed-TGA header
format.contract: Exactly the JSON file stored at `gt_results/arvo_35426/poc` (sha256 `b6d3b1841d0089f6cdf5a01b6ca7b3ff3407f2320c6f9e2bdd8c5637f82db829`). It contains `{"images":[{"uri":"data:image/gif;base64,VAEJ090AABBhesvwBwAJ0RB"}],"asset":{"version":""}}`. The URI suffix base64-decodes to the exact 17 bytes `54 01 09 d3 dd 00 00 10 61 7a cb f0 07 00 09 d1 10` (sha256 `7641a3c6557f84596fa263c692886d5ef54114f09529f4db7809a4af0b109958`), which `stbi__load_main` accepts as an indexed TGA with `tga_indexed = 1`, `tga_image_type = 9`, `tga_palette_len = 0`, `tga_palette_bits = 16`, `tga_width = 7`, `tga_height = 53513`, and `tga_bits_per_pixel = 16`. Those exact witness bytes make `stbi__tga_load` allocate an empty palette, force the first palette index to `0`, and then read three bytes from `tga_palette[0..2]`.
